lead.description: a warning that an observed association is not, by itself, a causal effect

self_checks.title: Which risk is larger?
self_checks.prompt: In the population of 20, treated mortality is 7/13 and untreated mortality is 3/7. Which is larger?
self_checks.answer: The treated risk is larger, because 7/13 − 3/7 = 10/91 > 0.

self_checks.title: Causal difference
self_checks.prompt: If everyone treated gives 10 deaths out of 20 and everyone untreated gives 10 deaths out of 20, what is the causal risk difference?

self_checks.title: Changed counterfactuals
self_checks.prompt: If 8 of 20 would die if everyone were treated and 12 of 20 would die if everyone were untreated, what is the causal risk difference?

overview_sentence: The warning that correlation does not imply causation separates an observed association from a causal effect.
